visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 at least shows the correct arithmetic-sum-to-area structure with (4k−1), multiplying by π, and total n(2n+1)π, whereas Lesson 1 is essentially blank at the title and its mid-frame formula/subtitles are malformed and visually fail to represent the intended computation clearly.

interactivity.rationale: Both lessons have no available gate specs or plan JSON, so neither shows any functioning checkpoints or input-rendering interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 is consistently clear and correctly spoken despite being verbose, while Lesson 1 has noticeable narration defects such as the garbled 'Thirth 2' and awkward '64 circles in total whole.'

sync.rationale: Both lessons are external transcripts without any beat or visual-cue timing data, so neither demonstrates better or worse alignment between narration references and on-screen changes.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 is more pedagogically effective because it carefully builds the k-th ring formula, summation, inequality, and final conversion from rings to circles, while Lesson 1 is mathematically correct but much more compressed and less supportive for a first-time learner, though Lesson 2 has a minor potentially confusing phrase about planting the compass at the shared point.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 is much more polished with centered, legible titles, clean consistent notebook-style layouts and readable cards, whereas Lesson 1 opens on an empty screen and later shows a poorly composed frame with awkward/gibberish subtitle text despite a large formula.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner. Four high-confidence agents favored Lesson 2: visual accuracy, narration quality, concept accuracy, and polish. These judgments emphasized that Lesson 2 presents the arithmetic-area structure more clearly, has cleaner and more readable visuals, stronger narration, and a more supportive mathematical explanation. The two tie verdicts were for interactivity and sync, where neither lesson showed evidence of functioning checkpoints or timing alignment data. No dimension favored Lesson 1, so the tied dimensions do not outweigh Lesson 2's strong advantages.
